questions.q: What three elements together make up a network?
options: A server, a switch, and a router
Devices, links, and a shared protocol
A LAN, a WAN, and the internet
Packets, headers, and addresses
questions.explain: A network needs devices that want to exchange data, links connecting them, and a shared protocol so the data means the same thing to both ends.

questions.q: Why does a message get broken into packets instead of sent as one continuous stream?
options: It is required by law for internet traffic
Packets allow a network's links to be shared efficiently among many conversations, with pieces reassembled using header information
Packets travel faster than a continuous stream over the same link
It makes the message unreadable to anyone but the sender
questions.explain: Splitting data into packets, each carrying sequence information in its header, lets multiple conversations share the same links efficiently and still be reassembled correctly.

questions.q: Northbridge Retail's warehouse network, confined to one building and owned entirely by Northbridge, is an example of what?
options: A WAN
The internet
A LAN
A packet
questions.explain: A Local Area Network (LAN) is a network confined to one site and controlled by a single organization — exactly what Northbridge's warehouse network is.

questions.q: What connects Northbridge Retail's warehouse LAN to its corporate office LAN across town?
options: A WAN link
A second internet
A packet header
A protocol
questions.explain: A Wide Area Network (WAN) link connects separate LANs, typically over a greater distance and often leased from an internet service provider.

questions.q: What does every device on a network need in order to send or receive data successfully?
options: A fixed, dedicated line reserved only for its traffic
An address that identifies it and a path to reach the destination
A direct physical cable to every other device on the network
Permission from the internet's central authority
questions.explain: Every device needs a unique address so data knows where to go, and a path — direct or through intermediate devices — to actually get there.
